question: Which of the following institutions is called 'lender of last resort'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**RBI**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **RBI** (Reserve Bank of India) is known as the 'lender of last resort'.
 
• The term signifies that the RBI provides financial assistance to banks and other institutions in times of financial distress or crisis.
 
• When banks face severe liquidity issues and are unable to obtain funds from any other source, they turn to the RBI for support.
 
• RBI's role as the lender of last resort helps maintain stability in the financial system and prevents bank failures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Reserve Bank of India** was established on April 1, 1935, in accordance with the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• The central office of the RBI was initially established in Calcutta but was permanently moved to Mumbai in 1937.
 
• RBI regulates and supervises the financial system, manages foreign exchange, and operates the currency and credit system of the country.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the development strategy of the Government of India.
 
• RBI also acts as the banker to the Government and maintains the accounts of the central and state governments.
